title: Pade Theory applied to the vacuum polarization of a heavy quark
claims_overlap: Reconstruction of the vacuum polarization from its low-energy expansion; extraction of threshold information.
equations_checked: Pade approximants built from the q^2->0 Taylor coefficients of Pi(q^2); extraction of the threshold constant K^(2).

read_level: equation level, eqs. (11)-(14) on p. 5 (read 23 October 2026; reports/LITERATURE_READS_2026-10-22.md)
exact_overlap: Threshold information IS extracted from the low-energy moments of the vacuum polarization. Pade approximants to a Stieltjes series are equivalent to Gaussian quadrature / orthogonal polynomials / Hankel determinants, i.e. the same classical machinery as our Theorem E. Eqs. (12)-(14) also use a negative Hankel determinant of Taylor coefficients, D(0,1) = -0.0226 < 0, to show that the O(alpha_s^2) term alone is not Stieltjes although the full function is: the falsifier use of the hierarchy.
exact_difference: They estimate a threshold-expansion constant by Pade fitting in q^2; we prove a one-sided bound in a radial variable. Their observable is Pi(q^2); ours is delta(r). Their falsifier acts on Taylor coefficients at q^2 = 0; ours on local moments of a position-space profile.
notes: Kills novelty of 'threshold from VP moments' and of 'Hankel determinant as Stieltjes falsifier' as such. Cited for both.

title: Effective Lagrangians and low-energy photon-photon scattering

(13)-(14) reproduce ours exactly; if the factor is theirs, it entered their omega^8 expansion before both Table II and eq. (15). Their note [10] two-loop factor 1 + (186685/17514) alpha/pi equals 2 d2 - (40/139)(d1 - d2) with Ritus's d1 = 40/9, d2 = 1315/252; the weights of the unpolarized cross section give 2 d2 + (40/139)(d1 - d2) = 25555/2502 (note E4, Section 11.3).
